subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should device-less non-local shared-token WebSocket clients ever receive operator scopes, and if so should that trust come from configured token scopes, device pairing, or another bounded policy?
rationale: The source-reproducible failure is real, but the repair changes whether a shared Gateway token can grant write/admin-like operator authority over a network connection.

options.title: Bounded Token Scopes
options.body: Land a reviewed `gateway.auth.tokenScopes`-style policy with non-loopback and privileged-scope safeguards, docs, and real WebSocket proof.

options.title: Require Device Pairing
options.body: Keep current scope clearing as the security boundary and document that non-local operator clients must pair or use a named trust path.

options.title: Trust Declared Scopes
options.body: Allow valid shared-token clients to keep self-declared scopes, accepting the broader network token authority model.

recommendation.title: Bounded Token Scopes
recommendation.body: Land a reviewed `gateway.auth.tokenScopes`-style policy with non-loopback and privileged-scope safeguards, docs, and real WebSocket proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This account owns the current tokenScopes proposal and recent shared-auth baseline work, making it the best available routing target for the product/security choice.
